findings.problem: The proof turns a finite density root `r` with `|1 - ‖r‖^2| < δ` into a unit vector `c • r`, where `c = ‖r‖⁻¹`. It then checks four things in turn: (i) the norm is 1, (ii) positivity is preserved via `smul_nonneg`, (iii) the finite-range submodule is preserved via `F.smul_mem`, and (iv) the squared left/right-unitary defect rescales by `‖r‖⁻²`, which is below `2δ` because `‖r‖^2 > 1/2`. Lines 56-109 (`hm`, `hr2`, `hr`, `c`, `z` and the four bullets) repeat the corresponding block of `expectation_unit_intertwiners` in NormalizedExpectationRoots.lean (`hm`, `hr2`, `hr`, the same `c`/`z` and the four bullets) almost line for line. Two things differ: the test family (`Unit` vs `Option I`) and the arithmetic step that gives `hb`. The 10-line derivation of `hm` from the trace-of-1 test, via `τ.normalized`, `inner_self_eq_norm_sq`, `densityRoot_norm` and `finiteVectorDensityTensor_norm_sq`, is also copied. So any change to the normalization argument has to be made in two files.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two lemmas to NormalizedExpectationRoots.lean, which the target already imports. Then rewrite both theorems to use them.

(1) `unit_normalization`: for `r : NuclearUltrapower.HilbertSchmidt H`, `δ ≤ 1/2` and `|1 - ‖r‖^2| < δ`, `0 ≤ hsOperator r`, and a finite-range submodule `F` for `r`, let `z := (((‖r‖⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ)) • r`. The conclusion is `1/2 < ‖r‖^2`, `‖z‖ = 1`, `0 ≤ hsOperator z`, the same `F` works for `z`, and for every `U` with `‖hsConjugation U r - r‖^2 < δ` we have `‖hsConjugation U z - z‖^2 < 2*δ`.
   Proof sketch: it is the current block. Get `1/2 < ‖r‖^2` by `linarith` from `abs_lt`, then `0 < ‖r‖`. Use `norm_smul` with `Complex.norm_real` and `inv_mul_cancel₀`. Use `map_smul` with `smul_nonneg`. Use `F.smul_mem`. For the last part use `map_smul`, `← smul_sub`, `norm_smul`, `inv_mul_lt_iff₀` and `nlinarith [mul_pos hδ (sub_pos.mpr hr2)]`, with `δ > 0` taken from `|1-‖r‖^2| < δ`.

(2) `norm_sq_eq_of_trace_one_test`: from `|(τ.functional 1).re - ∑ k, w k * (inner ℂ (x k) (x k)).re| < δ`, deduce `|1 - ‖densityRoot (finiteVectorDensityTensor w x)‖^2| < δ`. This is the 8-line `hm` proof.

Rewritten uses:
- In `expectation_normalized_spatial_vectors`, after `obtain` and the `change`s, run `have hm := norm_sq_eq_of_trace_one_test τ w hw x (ha none)`. Then `obtain ⟨hr2, hzn, hzp, hzF, hzU⟩ := unit_normalization r hδhalf hm hrp hrs`, and `refine ⟨_, hzn, hzp, hzF, ?_, fun j => by rw [hsLeft_sub_right_norm]; exact hzU _ (hru j)⟩`. Only the `normalized_quadratic_error` bullet stays, since it needs `a i`.
- In `expectation_unit_intertwiners`, use `δ := min (ε/4) (1/2)`, so `δ ≤ 1/2`. Use `ha ()` for `hm` and `hru j` for the defect. Then `2δ ≤ ε/2 < ε` closes the goal. This theorem becomes about 15 lines.
findings.benefit: The unit-normalization and finite-rank/positivity preservation are proved once, with a precise statement, instead of in two ~45-line copies. The target theorem then shows only what is specific to it, the self-adjoint test estimate. A fix to the normalization would be made in one place. A reader can see that the two theorems share one mechanism and differ only in their error bookkeeping.
